L85: # B.S. in Healthcare Management
L86: ## Program Overview
L87: 
L88: 【46†Return to the School of Business and Management Homepage†www.tesu.edu】
L89: 
L90: The Bachelor of Science (B.S.) degree program in Healthcare Management a 120-credit program. It is appropriate for students who wish to work or are currently working in responsible management positions in a wide variety of medical and healthcare institutions and organizations, physicians' group practices, and voluntary and governmental agencies.
L91: What Students Will Learn in the B.S. Degree in Healthcare Management
L92: 
L93: The B.S. degree in Healthcare Management is designed to provide students with the managerial skills, attitudes, and knowledge needed for administrative/management careers in the healthcare field.
L94: 
L95: All students in the B.S. degree in Healthcare Management program must complete a Business Administration Capstone requirement that integrates content across the degree program and validates the student's knowledge.
L96: 
L97: Degree Requirements
L98:   * College Algebra within Intellectual and Practical Skills section of general education requirements
L99:   * Quantitative Skills for Business and Statistics within the requirements of the Professional Business Requirements section
L100:   * How Students Earn Credit in the Area of Study: Courses in this area of study may be completed with Thomas Edison State University courses and/or courses from other institutionally accredited colleges. Prior learning assessment (PLA), and/or examinations may also be used.
L101: School of Business and Management Upper-Level Degree Policy
L102: 
L103: Require that baccalaureate students complete a minimum of 18 credits at the upper level (3000 level or higher). Complete 12 upper-level credits in the area of study, the Capstone, and one additional 3 credit course, which can be completed in the area of study or the Business Core.
L104: 
L105: NOTE:
L106: Courses that are devoid of a course code can be accepted in transfer if completed at colleges and universities accredited by the institutional accrediting agencies recognized by the U.S. Department of Education.
L107: 
L108: In addition, the University offers a host of ways to earn credit for knowledge obtained in non-collegiate settings. Examples include:
L109:   * Courses and examinations approved through National College Credit Recommendation Service (NCCRS) and the American Council on Education (ACE) College Credit Recommendation Service.
L110:   * Military service
L111:   * License and certifications
L112:   * Prior learning assessment (PLA)
